page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g is a general-purpose server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a 1 GB network-attached volume, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance alongside moderate multi-threaded capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in single-core stress-ng CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests indicate average performance, with read-only small block cached speeds at 439.02 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 41.08 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores align with the middle 50% of tested systems.

For specialized workloads, the server handles small-model LLM inference at average speeds, though prompt processing for medium-sized 7B models drops to the bottom 10% tier. Database operations and Redis SET performance remain in the average tier, processing 8.04 million operations per second. Given the dedicated AMD EPYC cores and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server is configured for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, single-threaded data processing, and lightweight database operations.
description: The Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g is a general-purpose virtual server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz, this configuration utilizes 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. It includes 1 GB of network-attached storage and one public IPv4 address, with no GPU hardware. Performance benchmarks show top-tier single-core CPU execution and single-threaded compression speeds, while multi-threaded decompression and memory bandwidth fall into average tiers. LLM inference on medium models presents a performance bottleneck, particularly during prompt processing. This server is suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, Redis caching, and database operations that benefit from dedicated CPU resources without requiring massive multi-threaded scaling.
